h1: The 6 Best Outdoor Storage Sheds for Bigger Budgets, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Outdoor Storage Shed Up to $1500: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 outdoor storage sheds from 24 to 96 square feet, resin and metal, compared on size, lockable doors, floors and weather.
summary: The DAUSOLA 8x12 ft metal shed is the best outdoor storage shed for a bigger budget, with about 96 square feet of floor for mowers, bikes and a workbench. The EASYHAWK 6x8 ft resin shed adds a window and lockable door, the Aoxun 7.3 by 5.3 ft steel shed is the mid-size value pick, and the Gizoon 6x4.4 ft is the compact resin choice.
intro: With a budget approaching $1500 the temptation is to buy the nicest shed. The smarter move is to buy the biggest one your yard and local rules allow, because the cost per square foot falls as the building grows and nobody ever complains that their shed is too empty. Most owners regret size long before they regret material.

This ranking sorts six sheds by footprint, material and security features. We reviewed the specifications supplied, which for several listings amount to size, colour and a material note, and we say plainly where details are missing. Smaller 5x3 and 6.2x4 ft models were left out as they do not suit a larger budget.

products.name: DAUSOLA 8x12 FT Outdoor Storage Shed, Metal Garden Tool Sheds for Backyard
products.verdict: An 8 by 12 ft metal shed, the roomiest building in this ranking.
products.description:
The DAUSOLA is an 8 by 12 foot metal garden shed with about 96 square feet of floor area. It is the largest unit here by a wide margin.

That size is why it wins. Ninety-six square feet takes a ride-on mower, a workbench, shelving and bikes without playing Tetris, and it can double as a hobby workshop. Metal construction resists rot and insects, and large metal sheds are commonly bolted down to a prepared base. The listing says little about floor or door lock details, so confirm those before you order.

Buy it if you want a real outbuilding. Skip it if your yard cannot host an 8 by 12 foot base.
products.idealFor: Owners wanting a true outbuilding for mower and tools.

products.name: EASYHAWK 6x8 FT Resin Storage Shed with Floor, Window & Lockable Door
products.verdict: A 6 by 8 ft resin shed with a floor, a window and a lockable door.
products.description:
The EASYHAWK is a 6 by 8 foot resin shed, around 48 square feet, with a floor, a window and a lockable door. It sits in the $500 and up price bucket.

It ranks second because it ticks the practical boxes in one package: the floor protects stored items, the window brings daylight so you can find things, and the lock secures tools. Resin does not rust, paint or rot. It has half the area of the DAUSOLA, but it is easier to fit into a typical yard.

Choose it for a tidy, secure, low-maintenance shed. Skip it if you need to store large machines.
cons: Half the area of the DAUSOLA

products.name: Aoxun 7.3'x5.3' Shed with Floor Galvanized Steel Outdoor Storage Shed Brown
products.verdict: A 7.3 by 5.3 ft galvanized steel shed with a built-in floor, in brown.
products.description:
The Aoxun is a galvanized steel shed of 7.3 by 5.3 feet with a built-in floor, giving roughly 39 square feet. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks third because it delivers the best space-for-price ratio among the mid-size options, at a fraction of the cost of the larger buildings. Galvanized steel resists rot and insects, and the built-in floor means less base prep than a floorless shed. It trails the EASYHAWK because the listing does not mention a window or a lock.

Buy it if you want proven steel and a floor for less. Skip it if you want a window.
products.idealFor: Tool and mower storage on a moderate budget.
products.skipIf: You want a window and a lock.

products.name: Gizoon 6x4.4 FT Resin Storage Shed with Floor, Outdoor Plastic Shed, Grey
products.verdict: A 6 by 4.4 ft resin shed with a floor, for small gardens.
products.description:
The Gizoon is a 6 by 4.4 foot resin shed with a floor, in grey. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks fourth because it is a good small shed that does not take advantage of a larger budget. At about 26 square feet, it suits hand tools, bikes and a few bins, but not a mower and workbench. The resin build is low maintenance, and the floor keeps stored items dry.

Choose it if your yard is small. Skip it if you want more space.

products.name: Patiowell 6x4 FT Resin Outdoor Storage Shed with Floor, Light Gray
products.verdict: A 6 by 4 ft light gray resin shed with a floor.
products.description:
The Patiowell is a 6 by 4 foot resin shed with a floor, in light gray. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks fifth because it is slightly smaller than the Gizoon, at 24 square feet. The light colour reflects heat, which helps in hot climates. Like the other small resin sheds, it is best for hand tools and garden gear.

Buy it for a light, heat-reflecting shed. Skip it if you need more depth.

products.name: Aoxun 4×6 FT All-Weather Resin Storage Shed, Dark Gray
products.verdict: A 4 by 6 ft dark gray all-weather resin shed.
products.description:
The Aoxun is a 4 by 6 foot all-weather resin shed in dark gray. It is in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It ranks last because it is the smallest and the listing mentions no floor. Dark resin absorbs heat, so site it out of full afternoon sun. It is still a fair option for tight spaces, and the all-weather resin build is low maintenance.

Choose it for a tight corner. Skip it if you want room to grow.

whatMatters.detail: A larger shed needs a bigger, level base and may need a permit. Check local rules for size limits and boundary distances. Measure the area, including room to open the door.
Metal sheds are stronger and larger, but can dent and rust at scratches. Resin sheds do not rust, but are generally smaller and can warp in extreme heat. Choose by size and climate.
A floor keeps items dry and lets you place the shed on gravel. Without a floor you need a concrete slab or wooden base. Check the listing for with floor.
A window lets in daylight so you can see inside, and a lockable door protects tools. If the listing does not mention them, assume you will add a padlock and no window.
Large sheds catch wind. Anchor them to the base with the supplied fixings, and add extra anchors in exposed sites. Follow the assembly instructions closely.

howToChoose.intro: More budget should mean more floor, not just a nicer finish.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a large shed?
faq.a: Often yes above a certain size. Rules vary widely, so ask your local authority about size limits, height and boundary distances before you buy.
Buying too small. Sheds fill quickly, and moving up a size later means starting again. Measure your contents and choose one size up.

faq.q: Is the DAUSOLA worth it over the EASYHAWK?
faq.a: If you need space, yes. If you need a window and lock in a tidy footprint, the EASYHAWK is better.
Large sheds take a full weekend with two or three people. Plan the base first, and use a calm day for panels.

faq.q: How do I maintain a metal shed?
faq.a: Keep the roof clear, touch up scratches with rust-resistant paint and check anchors each season.

faq.q: Can I add shelving or power?
faq.a: Shelving is usually fine if you fix into the frame. Power should be installed by a licensed electrician following local codes.

finalTake: The DAUSOLA 8x12 ft metal shed is the best outdoor storage shed for a larger budget, with about 96 square feet of floor. The EASYHAWK 6x8 ft resin shed is the secure, low-maintenance alternative with a window and lock, and the Aoxun 7.3 by 5.3 ft steel shed is the value mid-size option. Buy the largest shed your base and local rules allow.
